organization: American Society of Agronomy / Crop Science Society of America / Soil Science Society of America
document_title: Statement of Ethics and Code of Conduct
notes: Code of Conduct approved December 2025 by ASA, CSSA, SSSA Boards; Statement of Ethics (2024) is foundational document. Both required as condition of membership. Ethics Committee will detail investigation process in 2026.

organization: American Registry of Professional Animal Scientists
notes: ARPAS is the professional certification affiliate of the American Society of Animal Science (ASAS). Code of ethics is mandatory for board certification. Covers livestock, poultry, and companion animal science professionals.

document_title: IFA Members' Commitments / 12 Safety, Health and Environment Principles
notes: Protect & Sustain Certification (2012) is the de facto global product stewardship standard. 12 SHE Principles adopted by all IFA members. Covers safety, health, environment, anti-corruption.

organization: IFOAM — Organics International (International Federation of Organic Agriculture Movements)
notes: Four principles: Health, Ecology, Fairness, Care. Adopted by IFOAM General Assembly September 25, 2005. Explicitly normative/ethical framework underpinning global organic agriculture movement. Implemented through national certification standards.

organization: National FFA Organization (Future Farmers of America)
notes: 9-pledge code adopted by delegates at 1952 National FFA Convention. Covers courtesy, honesty, respect, sportsmanship, FFA program participation. Chapter-level enforcement. FFA represents ~700,000 agricultural youth members.

document_title: Code of Practice on Safety and Health in Agriculture
notes: Adopted by international expert group October 2010; endorsed by ILO Governing Body March 2011. Complements Safety and Health in Agriculture Convention C184 (2001) and Recommendation R192. Covers 26 topics. Agriculture employs ~1 billion workers worldwide.

document_title: Fair Chase Statement and Hunter and Conservation Ethics
notes: Fair Chase concept originates from 5th article of B&C constitution (1888), the earliest known use of the term. Modern statement defines fair chase as ethical, sportsmanlike, lawful pursuit not giving improper advantage over game. Signed affidavit required for trophy record submissions.

Bowhunting-specific application of fair chase ethics. Defines fair chase as ethical, sportsmanlike, lawful pursuit not giving improper/unfair advantage. Takes strong stance against certain technologies (remote scouting, real-time GPS tracking). Fair Chase Affidavit required for records submission.

Adopted by member referendum November 3, 2000; replaced code from 1976 (amended 1986, 1992). Four core pledges: Service and Stewardship, Sound Science, Honesty and Integrity, Communication and Transparency. Bylaws specify reprimand, censure, expulsion as possible sanctions.

First adopted 1976; revised 1992, 2015. 28 canons covering relationships with clients, employers, public, and other foresters. All membership categories required to abide as condition of membership. Complaint procedures via ACF National Office.

ICF received Royal Charter 1982; only UK body conferring Chartered Forester and Chartered Arboriculturist titles. Code of Conduct 2015. Binding on all members with CPD obligations. Emphasizes competence, integrity, trust, and public safety.

document_title: FSC Principles and Criteria for Forest Stewardship
notes: 10 Principles covering legal compliance, worker wellbeing, Indigenous peoples' rights, community relations, forest management, environmental values, management plan, monitoring, high conservation values, plantation management. Third-party certification; FSC trademark requires compliance. ~200M ha globally certified.

organization: Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification
notes: World's largest forest certification system (~300M ha). Endorses 48 national/regional systems. Three sustainability pillars: ecological, social responsibility, economic viability. Particularly serves small and family forest owners. Third-party assessment against PEFC Sustainability Benchmarks.

Covers responsibilities to aquatic resources, public, employers, peers, and the profession. Includes provisions on scientific misconduct, coercion by employers, diversity and inclusion. Misconduct reported to Executive Director, AFS President, and/or Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee. Also has separate Meetings Code of Conduct.

organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
document_title: Code of Conduct for Responsible Fisheries
notes: Adopted by FAO Conference Resolution 4/95 on October 31, 1995. Voluntary but most cited global fisheries ethics instrument. Global and comprehensive scope. Underpins 4 international plans of action, 2 strategies, 28 technical guidelines. Covers conservation, management, fishing operations, aquaculture, post-harvest practices, trade, research.

Current version: 3.1 (July 2024). Three principles: Sustainable Fish Stocks, Minimal Environmental Impact, Effective Management. 28 performance indicators scored 0-100 (80+ = certification). Voluntary application; MSC ecolabel conditioned on certification. Most widely recognized sustainable seafood standard.

Adopted 2007; entered into force November 16, 2017. Applies to all fishers on commercial fishing vessels. Covers: minimum age, work agreements, accommodation and food, medical care, working time, repatriation, social protection, occupational safety and health. Legally binding for ratifying states.
